history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - a Vaishnavite satra (monastery), not a conventional temple; keep-or-drop decision needed. Sri Sri Auniati Satra on Majuli island was founded in 1653 CE with the patronage of Ahom king Jayadhwaj Singha; the first satradhikar was Sri Sri Niranjana Deva Goswami. It is one of the four 'raj satras' (royal satras) and follows the Brahma Sanghati of the Ekasarana Dharma of Srimanta Sankaradeva; Krishna is worshipped as Govinda and monks are celibate udaseen Vaishnavas trained in Sattriya dance, bhaona theatre and khol/taal. The name comes from an 'Auni paan' (betel creeper) at the elevated 'ati' where it was established. The 371-year continuous tradition of Paal Naam was celebrated in November 2024, drawing around three lakh devotees. CSV town 'Jorhat' is WRONG: the satra is on Majuli river island (Majuli district), reached via ferry from Nimati Ghat near Jorhat. Wikipedia coordinates (26.9402, 94.1238) are corroborated by geocoding (26.93685, 94.12368).

name: Sri Sri Auniati Satra
town_description: Majuli is the world's largest inhabited river island, on the Brahmaputra in Assam. It is the seat of Assamese Neo-Vaishnavite culture, home to historic satras, Sattriya dance and mask-making, reached by ferry from Nimati Ghat near Jorhat.

travel.airport: Jorhat Airport (JRH), about 20 km to Nimati Ghat, then a ferry to Majuli
travel.railway: Jorhat Town railway station, about 7 km to Nimati Ghat; ferries run to Kamalabari/Aphalamukh on Majuli
travel.road: Road from Jorhat town to Nimati Ghat (15-20 km), then ferry across the Brahmaputra; Majuli can also be reached via the Bogibeel Bridge route

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Raas Mahotsav (October/November) is the peak festival season
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented; the naam-ghar is the prayer hall, visitors should respect satra discipline (celibate monks, no footwear in the premises)
